Abdul Wahab (Md) ------ Petitioner
Vs.
State & another ------ Opposite-Parties
full_judgment: 7. It appears from the FIR and charge-sheet that there is specific allegation against the accused-petitioner that he submitted wealth statement by concealing some properties and thereby committed offence under section 26(2) and also acquisition of some properties specified therein were found disproportionate to his known source of income attracting another offence under section 27(1) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act. The charge-sheet has clearly specified the properties along with value of the same which was concealed in the wealth statement and the properties along with value, which were found disproportionate to his known source of income. These are allegations against the accused-petitioner brought by the prosecution. Though the accused-petitioner does not admit those allegation to be true, the disputed facts are not supposed to be resolved in this forum. The accused-petitioner shall get opportunity to explain about the acquisition of property so concealed and his legal sources of income justifying acquisition of properties found in his possession at the time of trial by adducing evidence. Section 27(2) clearly provides that the accused shall have to rebut presumption about the allegation and explain his position as to the acquisition of properties disclosing source of income. Therefore, mere denial of allegation cannot be taken into consideration in the present proceeding under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Thus we find that since there are specific allegations against the accused-petitioner attracting elements of offences under section 26(2) and 27(1) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004, the question of quashing the proceeding on mere denial of such allegations does not arise.
